\begin{document}
\section{Adversarial \emph{Math} \& $x^2$ Cases}
\label{sec:adv}
\begin{equation}\label{eq:one} a=1 \end{equation}
Tagged (counter must NOT advance):
\begin{equation} b=2 \tag{B} \end{equation}
This must print (2):
\begin{equation}\label{eq:two} c=3 \end{equation}
Align with ALL rows nonumber (expect ZERO events):
\begin{align}
  u &= 1 \nonumber \\
  v &= 2 \nonumber
\end{align}
Subequations:
\begin{subequations}
\begin{equation}\label{eq:sub-a} s_1=1 \end{equation}
\begin{equation} s_2=2 \end{equation}
\end{subequations}
Aligned inside equation (expect ONE event):
\begin{equation}\label{eq:aligned}
\begin{aligned} p &= 1 \\ q &= 2 \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Eqref in prose: \eqref{eq:one}. Refs: \ref{sec:adv}.
A citation \citep{knuth1984texbook} and another \citet[see][chap.~2]{lamport1994latex}.
\begin{thebibliography}{9}
\bibitem{knuth1984texbook} D.~E. Knuth, \emph{The TeXbook}, 1984.

\end{thebibliography}
